model.name: Resilience Maturity
model.description: H.4 — a dedicated, cmdash-authored maturity ladder for recovery capability: whether an organization's DECLARED Recovery Time/Point Objectives (RTO/RPO) for its crown-jewel systems (Asset.declaredRtoMinutes/declaredRpoMinutes) are backed by TESTED recovery evidence, not just policy on paper. Same 'declared vs tested' shape O.6 established for control efficacy (attested vs validated), applied to a different capability. A single-dimension model kept separate from the broader Recover function so a tenant's actual, measured recovery capability is independently drillable rather than blended into a coarser control family. Maps to NIST CSF 2's RC.RP (Incident Recovery Plan Execution) category so both an attested crosswalk baseline (via ControlAssessment on RC.RP-05/RC.RP-03) and live telemetry (tenant-submitted recovery-drill results, observationType=RECOVERY_TEST_RESULT) can seed and score the same dimension. cmdash's own production database restore drill (docs/runbooks/database-restore.md) is the first real recording against this dimension.

levels.name: Undeclared
levels.description: Crown-jewel systems carry no declared RTO/RPO targets, or targets exist only in an offline document no one maintains. Recovery capability, if any, has never been measured against a stated objective.

levels.name: Declared
levels.description: Crown-jewel systems have explicit RTO/RPO targets recorded (Asset.declaredRtoMinutes/declaredRpoMinutes), but no recovery drill has ever measured whether those targets are actually achievable. The declaration is a claim, not yet evidence.

levels.name: Tested
levels.description: At least one recovery drill has been performed and recorded (RECOVERY_TEST_RESULT) against each crown-jewel system's declared target within the current freshness window, with a written runbook of what actually happened — not just what was planned.

levels.name: Proven
levels.description: Recovery drills are performed on a fixed, recurring cadence, consistently meet the declared RTO/RPO (or the declared target has been honestly revised to match measured reality), and a drill failure demonstrably triggers a runbook update and a re-test — the program closes the loop from measurement to correction to re-measurement, the same discipline H.1's Adaptive tier describes for human risk.

dimensions.name: Recovery Resilience
dimensions.description: Whether a crown-jewel Asset's declared RTO/RPO target is backed by a tested recovery result, normalized by the shared `normalizeObservation` curve (packages/shared/src/maturity/telemetry.ts, observationType=RECOVERY_TEST_RESULT) — PASS when the drill met both declared targets, PARTIAL when it met one, FAIL when it met neither. An asset with a declared target and no drill on file contributes no telemetry (not a fabricated FAIL) — see RecoveryTestResultService.mapRecoveryTestOutcome.
